solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cleaner after food eats hot pot, well-cooked

indicators.note: food that is well cooked has been thoroughly worked over, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner tucks into a well-cooked hotpot before cleaning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-cooked' reshuffles the ten letters of EATS and HOT POT.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothpaste is what people use to clean their teeth after a meal.

clue.text: Cotton on back of carpet and rug

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so take the last of carpet

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig, a hairpiece

explanation.surface: Cotton threads lying on the back of a carpet and rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cotton on' looks like a fabric on top of the carpet but is the definition, meaning to grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on and to twig both mean to realise or understand, informal British idioms.

clue.text: Young officer picked up wine in French airport

indicators.note: the wine is placed inside the name of the airport

parts.note: Orly is one of the Paris airports

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: red is a wine

explanation.surface: A junior officer collected some wine at a Paris airport.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'picked up' reads upwards. An orderly is strictly a soldier serving an officer, so the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: An orderly is a junior soldier detailed to attend an officer, loosely a young military man.

clue.text: Prince mostly rational, taking no dope or weed?

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: lucid means clear-headed or rational
taken as written
dope is slang for information, as is gen

explanation.surface: A prince, mostly sensible, who refuses dope or weed.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, as is dope. The question mark flags weed as an example of a mind-altering drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis, called weed, can be classed as a drug that alters perception, with a question mark for the loose example.

clue.text: C & A situated in surprisingly dear shopping mall

indicators.note: the pair of letters is placed within the rearranged word
something turning out surprisingly is unexpected, so the letters of dear come in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written
the letters C and A; C&A is also a clothing store chain

explanation.surface: The C&A store is situated in an unexpectedly expensive shopping mall.
explanation.walkthrough: C&A is a clothing chain once common on British high streets, so the surface reads as a store in a mall.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade is a covered passage lined with shops, a kind of shopping precinct.

clue.text: University to put in pilot teaching session

indicators.note: the first pieces are put inside the word for pilot

parts.note: a pilot scheme is a trial
taken as written

explanation.surface: A university arranges to install a pilot teaching session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' looks like an aviator but means a test run, TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a small-group lesson with a tutor, a teaching session.

clue.text: Swell time away from work

parts.note: someone off is not at work

explanation.surface: It is lovely to have some time away from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like an adjective meaning great but is the noun for a smart, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell and a toff are both old slang for a fashionable, well-to-do gentleman.

clue.text: What should already have been paid in coppers

definitions.text: What should already have been paid

definitions.meaning: police officers, called the ... in British slang

explanation.surface: An overdue debt that was settled in small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' looks like pennies, fitting the payment, but means police; the Old Bill is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpaid earlier invoice is literally an aged bill, and police are nicknamed the same in Britain.

clue.text: Meet old man carrying gold, say

indicators.note: the outer word carries the other pieces within it

parts.note: old man is slang for father
or is the heraldic term for gold
e.g., for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: Meeting an elderly man who is carrying gold, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry; EG (for example) is what 'say' gives.
explanation.definitionFit: To foregather is to assemble or come together, an old verb for meeting.

clue.text: Coarse show includes blue material ultimately

indicators.note: the word for show has other letters included in it

parts.note: to indicate is to show

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A vulgar show featuring risqué material at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E and L, the last letters of blue and material, placed inside INDICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indelicate is crude or lacking refinement, a synonym for coarse.

clue.text: German banker rejected note after note

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters are read backwards
the second note is placed after the first

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
do is the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A German banker turned down one note after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a crossword term for a river, which has banks. REDO turned round by 'rejected' gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river forming part of Germany's eastern border, and a river has banks.

clue.text: Snazzy dresser in a shop left a mess

indicators.note: a shop left a mess has its contents jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A smart dresser in a boutique left the place untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a mess' reshuffles the twelve letters of IN A SHOP LEFT A.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashion plate is someone always dressed in the latest style, a stylish person.

clue.text: Brand-new opportunity in training

indicators.note: the opportunity sits inside the training word

parts.note: a grounding is basic training
a break is a chance or opportunity

explanation.surface: A fresh opening has arisen in the training programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opportunity' as a lucky break is the inserted piece; 'Brand-new' is the definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundbreaking work is innovative, never done before, so it is novel.

clue.text: One who is accepted as crazy?

indicators.note: crazy letters are wildly disordered, so the fodder is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who is widely regarded as being mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges ACCEPTED AS; the whole clue also describes such a dreamy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A space cadet is slang for an eccentric, absent-minded person, one who seems out of touch with reality.

clue.text: Effervescent-sounding old masseuse?

indicators.note: sounding means the word is said rather than spelt

parts.note: an effervescent drink is fizzy

explanation.surface: An elderly masseuse with a bubbly sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: a physiotherapist gives massage but is not strictly a masseuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A physio, short for physiotherapist, treats muscles with massage among other therapies.

clue.text: Swimmer talked of money a great deal

indicators.note: talked of means the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: cash is money
a lot means a great deal

explanation.surface: A swimmer who talked about money a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The French-derived first part is spelt CACH but pronounced like CASH.
explanation.definitionFit: The cachalot is the sperm whale, a huge marine creature that swims.

clue.text: A small house in dry coastal region

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed within the word for dry

parts.note: sere means dried up or withered

explanation.surface: A little house in an arid coastal area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' is the literary word for withered, not the opposite of wet sea air.
explanation.definitionFit: The seashore is the land along the edge of the sea, a coastal strip.

clue.text: Approves of prisoners getting executed inside

indicators.note: the executed word is placed inside the prisoners word

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners
done means carried out, executed

explanation.surface: Supports prisoners being executed while in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' suggests killing but just means carried out, DONE; 'inside' also hints at prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone something is to accept or overlook it, loosely to approve of it.

clue.text: In north country area, very blissful place

indicators.note: the very letter is placed in the country

parts.note: Iran is a country

explanation.surface: In a northern region of a country there is a very blissful spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link to the opening phrase but signals V going inside IRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist state of perfect peace, used loosely for any paradise.

clue.text: Item left inside car

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the car

parts.note: a coupe is a two-door car

explanation.surface: Something was left inside the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item' looks like an object left in the car but means a pair in a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who are an item are romantically together, a pair of lovers.

clue.text: Mushrooms raised in a single batch

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the pieces turns them to read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a crop is a batch produced at one time

explanation.surface: Mushrooms grown in one batch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns IN, I and CROP upwards to give the letters; 'raised' looks like growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcini are the Italian name for ceps, prized edible wild fungi.

clue.text: First of batsmen caught by seven stone player

indicators.note: the first letter is held within the Roman numeral, as if caught

parts.note: VII is seven in Roman numerals

indicators.note: First of picks the initial letter of batsmen

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A seven-stone cricketer catches the opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' suggests cricket, but just puts B inside VII.
explanation.definitionFit: A vibist plays the vibraphone, so is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Mules are short animals found aboard sailing vessels

indicators.note: the other pieces are on board, inside the ships word

parts.note: clippers are fast sailing ships

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written before shortening
pets are domestic animals

explanation.surface: Mules are said to be shortish animals carried aboard sailing ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mules' looks like the animals but means backless indoor shoes; 'short' trims the last letter of are.
explanation.definitionFit: Mules are backless indoor shoes, a type of soft house footwear.

clue.text: Evidence of work done by British composer

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics, so it measures work done

explanation.surface: Proof of a British composer's output.
explanation.walkthrough: The erg is a scientific unit of work; B for British joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: Thirsty shortly before noon, wanting this?

definitions.text: Thirsty shortly before noon, wanting this?

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: dry means thirsty
AM means before noon

explanation.surface: Feeling parched late in the morning and craving a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: someone thirsty in the morning may want a small whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram is a small measure of whisky, the drink a thirsty person might want.

clue.text: Thinking tumbledown cottage can accommodate one, plus four towards the back

indicators.note: a tumbledown building is falling apart, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order
the jumbled cottage letters can accommodate, or hold, the one within them
the four is set near the rear of the word, just before its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Pondering whether a ramshackle cottage can house one person and four more at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly, the jumbled cottage letters hold the one, giving a word for ponder, and 'towards the back' sets the four in just before that word's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cogitative means given to deep thought, from cogitate, to ponder.

clue.text: Drink dispenser used regularly in the east

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken from the following words

explanation.surface: A drinks machine in regular use in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of THE EAST, starting with the first, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A teat is a nipple on an udder or bottle that gives milk, a source of drink.

clue.text: Enduring endless sport and several operas

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to sport clothes is to wear them
The Ring is Wagner's cycle of four operas

explanation.surface: Putting up with ceaseless games and a stack of operas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' looks like games but is the verb to wear, cut to WEA; The Ring is Wagner's four-opera cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Weathering a storm means surviving it, so it is a synonym for withstanding.
